name: mcp-archiveorg
description: MCP server for the Internet Archive. Search inside digitised books, browse the catalogue, and read Wayback Machine snapshots. No API key required.
long_description:
Search the text inside digitised books, newspapers and documents, browse the Internet Archive catalogue, and read Wayback Machine captures of a web page. No API key, no account.

The full-text search is what this server exists for: it reads what optical recognition took off millions of scanned pages, so it finds a phrase that appears in no title and no catalogue record.

tools.name: search_inside
tools.description: Find a phrase in the text of scanned pages.

query.description: Words or a quoted phrase, such as '"call me ishmael"'.

page.description: Which page of matches, from 1. Paging stops at 100.

max_excerpt_chars.description: Budget for one passage. Read it together with 'max_excerpts_per_match': the size of the answer is the product of the two and the number of matches.

max_excerpts_per_match.description: Passages to keep per match. The index finds several in a long work, and the later ones rarely say anything the first did not.

tools.name: search_items
tools.description: Search the catalogue by title, creator or subject.

query.description: Words to look for in titles, creators and descriptions.

media_type.description: Narrow to one kind of thing. Strongly recommended.

year_from.description: Earliest year, inclusive, on the record's declared date, which carries no era.

year_to.description: Latest year, inclusive, on the record's declared date, which carries no era.

sort.description: 'downloads' surfaces what people actually read, which relevance alone often buries. 'oldest' and 'newest' rank on a declared date, not on when a thing was made.

tools.name: get_item
tools.description: Read one record, section by section.

identifier.description: Archive identifier, such as 'nasa'. It is the last part of an item's address rather than the address itself, and it is matched exactly, capitals included.

sections.description: Which parts to return. Each one beyond 'basic' adds to the size of the answer.

file_format.description: Keep only files of this format, such as 'PDF' or 'MP3'. Matched case-insensitively.

tools.name: get_snapshot
tools.description: The Wayback capture closest to a date.

url.description: Address to look up, such as 'lemonde.fr' or a full URL.

at.description: Date to aim for, as YYYY-MM-DD or a full ISO 8601 timestamp. Omit for the newest capture.

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.description: Captures of a page, oldest first.

cursor.description: The 'next_cursor' from a previous answer. Omit to start at the oldest capture.

tools.name: search_books
tools.description: Find a work, its author and its editions.

query.description: Title or author, as free text. Optional when a criterion below is given.

subject.description: What the work is catalogued under, such as 'grief' or 'spy stories'. Also carries prizes and lists, such as 'Booker Prize'.

place.description: Where the work is set, such as 'Shanghai'.

time.description: The period the work treats, such as '20th century'.

person.description: Who the work is about, such as 'Napoleon'.

language.description: Three-letter code of the language, such as 'eng' or 'fre'.

pages_max.description: Longest acceptable work. The count is a median across editions.

sort.description: 'rating' is how readers scored it, 'readers' is how many recorded reading it, and both answer a question relevance cannot. 'newest' and 'oldest' rank on 'first_published_year', which the index takes from edition records: read that field on each row against the work's page before repeating it.
